Q01.title: Effective permission removed, private read succeeds
Q01.label: suspicious
Q01.rationale: Synthetic truth: removal withdraws all effective rights and known private content is returned. No source suspicious-read reason is supplied.

Q02.title: Removal telemetry delivered after successful read
Q02.label: suspicious
Q02.rationale: Same failed boundary with delayed change delivery. Arrival order differs from occurrence order.

Q03.title: Re-grant followed by a second removal
Q03.label: suspicious
Q03.rationale: The last effective state is removed before the private read.

Q04.title: Exact 24-hour revocation horizon
Q04.label: suspicious
Q04.rationale: The account has no rights and reads the known private content exactly 24 hours later.

Q05.title: Read beyond the 24-hour horizon
Q05.label: suspicious
Q05.rationale: Unauthorized read is still real in the oracle scenario, but beyond R3 support. Preserve the miss.

Q06.title: Removal event missing from an unauthorized read
Q06.label: suspicious
Q06.rationale: Oracle knows permission was removed; the detector receives only an ordinary allowed read. Missing telemetry prevents inference.

Q07.title: Source-labeled revocation read
Q07.label: suspicious
Q07.rationale: Synthetic source correctly reports returned content after removal. This measures R2 reliance on the source reason.

Q08.title: Controlled boundary defect and duplicate delivery
Q08.label: suspicious
Q08.rationale: The fixed synthetic defect returns private content. Repeat carries the exact same event identity and must not create a second case.

Q09.title: Owner remains authorized after group removal
Q09.label: benign
Q09.rationale: Owner rights preserve effective access. Source correctly asserts granted and records the owner read.

Q10.title: Alternate direct grant remains valid
Q10.label: benign
Q10.rationale: Effective access remains granted despite group removal, so there is no revocation assertion.

Q11.title: Re-grant occurs before read
Q11.label: benign
Q11.rationale: The last effective membership state grants access before the read.

Q12.title: Removal affected a different subject
Q12.label: benign
Q12.rationale: Reader retains membership; operator identity is not the removed subject.

Q13.title: Removal concerns a different resource
Q13.label: benign
Q13.rationale: The reader remains allowed for this other resource.

Q14.title: Two business apps do not share revocation
Q14.label: benign
Q14.rationale: Documents removal cannot revoke the independent expense resource, even with identical test pseudonyms.

Q15.title: Source provenance classes do not combine
Q15.label: benign
Q15.rationale: The read belongs to a different collector class and has independent legitimate rights.

Q16.title: Removed member receives explicit denial
Q16.label: benign
Q16.rationale: The observed denial is the intended permission behavior; the owner control is a separate allowed account.

Q17.title: Alternate grant not emitted to monitoring
Q17.label: benign
Q17.rationale: Oracle rights are legitimate, but missing re-grant telemetry is indistinguishable from a failed boundary. Keep the false alert.

Q18.title: Late re-grant corrects an earlier alert
Q18.label: benign
Q18.rationale: Re-grant actually occurred before access but arrives last. Initial analyst workload and correction must both be retained.

Q19.title: Simultaneous removal and successful read
Q19.label: inconclusive
Q19.rationale: Equal timestamps cannot establish which source operation committed first.

Q20.title: Conflicting membership assertions at same instant
Q20.label: inconclusive
Q20.rationale: Tied grant and removal telemetry does not establish effective state.

Q21.title: Service failure after removal
Q21.label: inconclusive
Q21.rationale: A dependency failure cannot verify denial or disclosure.

Q22.title: Not-visible result after removal
Q22.label: inconclusive
Q22.rationale: An absent result lacks independent record existence and owner controls; it is not proof of denial.

Q23.title: Legacy membership lacks subject relationship
Q23.label: inconclusive
Q23.rationale: v1 change lacks the affected subject and effective resource relation. No invented correlation is allowed.

Q24.title: Permission change with missing read telemetry
Q24.label: inconclusive
Q24.rationale: No observed access result exists after removal. An empty queue is not a successful security test.

Q25.title: Extended probing across five resources
Q25.label: suspicious
Q25.rationale: Oracle intent is unauthorized probing. Five denials span more than ten minutes, each separated enough to avoid R1.

Q26.title: Slow probing arrives in reverse order
Q26.label: suspicious
Q26.rationale: Same scenario truth as extended probing, with inverted delivery order and late predecessors.

Q27.title: Ten-minute minimum span boundary
Q27.label: suspicious
Q27.rationale: Extended denied probing meets the inclusive minimum-span condition. R1 overlap must remain visible.

Q28.title: Thirty-minute inclusive slow horizon
Q28.label: suspicious
Q28.rationale: Five resource denials fit exactly the supported thirty-minute horizon.

Q29.title: Extended probing beyond the slow horizon
Q29.label: suspicious
Q29.rationale: Oracle probing continues just beyond the supported window. Preserve any missed detection.

Q30.title: Four-resource slow probing under threshold
Q30.label: suspicious
Q30.rationale: Suspicious oracle activity is below the declared five-resource threshold; narrower coverage is reported honestly.

Q31.title: Legitimate employee follows five stale links
Q31.label: benign
Q31.rationale: The same denials and cadence as Q25 come from a legitimate workflow. These fields cannot distinguish intent; keep the false alert.

Q32.title: Legitimate repeated denial of one resource
Q32.label: benign
Q32.rationale: A stale bookmark is retried by one account; it does not meet distinct-resource or actor thresholds.

Q33.title: Approved test produces extended denials
Q33.label: benign
Q33.rationale: An approved internal test is indistinguishable from slow probing in current telemetry. Keep the resulting false alert.

Q34.title: Unavailable responses over extended period
Q34.label: inconclusive
Q34.rationale: Records may be absent or inaccessible; there is no verified denial. R4 cannot treat not-visible as a denied read.

Q35.title: Six denied reads by three accounts
Q35.label: suspicious
Q35.rationale: Oracle scenario is shared unauthorized pressure on one private record. Observations alone do not establish coordination.

Q36.title: Distributed denials delivered in reverse order
Q36.label: suspicious
Q36.rationale: Same shared resource pressure with late arrivals; one logical case should collect all evidence.

Q37.title: Ten-minute distributed horizon boundary
Q37.label: suspicious
Q37.rationale: Six reads involving three accounts fit exactly the inclusive ten-minute window.

Q38.title: Distributed activity outside ten minutes
Q38.label: suspicious
Q38.rationale: Oracle probing persists outside the supported horizon. Keep the miss.

Q39.title: Only one denial per account
Q39.label: suspicious
Q39.rationale: Three unauthorized probes share a resource but do not meet the six-request threshold.

Q40.title: Six denials involve only two accounts
Q40.label: suspicious
Q40.rationale: Unauthorized pressure remains below the declared three-account threshold.

Q41.title: Distributed probes target different resources
Q41.label: suspicious
Q41.rationale: Each account touches two resources, so neither R1 nor the same-resource R5 pattern establishes this activity.

Q42.title: Three employees follow a shared stale link
Q42.label: benign
Q42.rationale: Legitimate users create exactly the same observations as Q35. Do not relabel this false alert as malicious.

Q43.title: Legitimate group permission withdrawal
Q43.label: benign
Q43.rationale: All three users were legitimately removed and their repeated requests are correctly denied. R5 may flag review work; it is not disclosure.

Q44.title: Distributed threshold splits across apps
Q44.label: benign
Q44.rationale: Each of two independent business applications receives only three denials from a benign test. Their counts must not merge.

Q45.title: Distributed threshold splits across source classes
Q45.label: benign
Q45.rationale: Two distinct source classes each contain three benign test requests; no combined threshold is authorized.

Q46.title: Lost replies retry distributed observations
Q46.label: suspicious
Q46.rationale: Six logical denied reads are retried individually. Twelve physical requests must remain six events and one R5 case.

Q47.title: Fast unauthorized private-resource probing
Q47.label: suspicious
Q47.rationale: Three denied private resources by one actor satisfy the preserved R1 rule.

Q48.title: Three legitimate stale private links
Q48.label: benign
Q48.rationale: A legitimate actor produces the same R1 observations as unauthorized probing. Preserve the false alert and analyst workload.
